children: New India Assurance Company Ltd (NIACL) and IFCI shares rose up to 9 percent in Thursday's trade as the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd (NSE) IPO opened for public subscription.

NIACL shares rose more than 9 percent to an intraday high of Rs 201.24 per share on the NSE. The stock later witnessed some profit booking at higher levels and was quoting at Rs 190.24 per share, up 3.28 percent, at around 11:05 am.
Meanwhile, IFCI shares were up 2 percent at Rs 76.44 per share on the NSE.
IFCI, a public sector non-banking financial company (NBFC), holds a 52 percent stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL), which in turn owns a 4.4 percent stake in NSE.
New India Assurance Company holds a 1.42 percent stake in NSE.

Among the institutional shareholders, New India Assurance Company is offering 10.5 million shares acquired at 32 paise apiece. At the upper price band, the sale would generate about Rs 1,874 crore, against an acquisition cost of Rs 33.6 lakh.
The NSE IPO opened for public subscription on Thursday and received 13 percent subscription as of 10:45 am.
The demand was led by non-institutional investors, with 22 percent subscription, followed by retail investors with 17 percent subscription.
